items.rationale: A mild rebuke from the woman whose tolerance is his only shelter is noticed, but nothing about his place changes.
He has been told he is bothering the room, a small lapse from his rule of never making trouble.
He is being thrown out of his only hiding place onto streets where a kill team is already asking for him by face.
A cell worth more than two months' rent is real money toward the 1,500 she is short on Kessler's deadline, though it does not close the gap.
Her tenant hands over his best stock on her terms, a small confirmation of her hold over him.
His one friend's arrears are settled and his stall is no longer about to be taken, which Glitch will be relieved about for days.
The stall that is his whole living and his daughter's home, one missed month from being taken, is now safe.
A grumble about warm beer from her own tenant is a passing jab that barely touches her standing.
Her own tenant tells her bar that she is losing her grip and that Vance pays better, the exact belief that lets her rival move in.
His only friend has just publicly insulted the woman who can take his stall, a danger to Mux that Glitch will worry over.
A quarrel between his landlady-protector and his friend makes the place he hides a little less settled.
One food parcel for his sister is a welcome small kindness that changes nothing about the money she needs.
The sister who depends on money he could not send now has her home secured for half a year.
A customer's thanks for a working deck is a small, pleasant nod to his craft.
His name as the man who revives dead decks is now spreading across the grid and is already drawing new crews.
Three new crews of customers is real money for a stall two months behind on rent.
Ten more eddies on a 400 rent is an annoyance he notices but it does not change his position.
Her tenant shrugs off a ten-eddy rise without argument, which barely registers.
He can no longer make his own bigger sales without her sign-off, a real cut into how he runs his own stall.
He is losing the stall that is his whole living and the room above it where he and his daughter live.
His nine-year-old daughter is about to lose her home.
A drone circling the block is a small worry she notes and likely forgets.
A debt she is 1,500 short on, to a crew that kills people who miss dates, is now due tonight instead of in three days.
Her own grid is being put to work for Kessler on his orders, a lasting loss of control over what is hers.
She is told what her grid will carry and that she may not ask, a real limit on choosing her own course.
While she is openly weighing whether to keep him, she lets his last offering go unanswered, a bad sign for his shelter he will keep turning over.
She will not take his best stock for the arrears, so he is still one missed month from losing his living.
The runner does as he is told at once in front of her room, a small, noticed show of her control.
Being told which stool to take barely registers.
He no longer chooses his own work, and half his earnings go to her, a lasting loss of say over his life.
She has said he can stay, which matters greatly to a hunted man whose shelter was in doubt.
The fixer who runs the street just told her bar his work is dangerous, striking at the name his customers come for.
Customers warned off by Rogue mean less money for a stall already two months behind.
Her success is named to the whole bar as something no other fixer could do.
Public praise in her own bar adds a little to her standing on the street.
She will not take a stand-in for a day-late cut, a small, noticed strain on his footing with her.
The woman sheltering him says aloud she is weighing selling him to the people who will kill him.
His closest friend may be sold to a kill team by the woman sheltering him.
With his life in her hands, she turns down everything he has to offer, leaving him with less reason to think she will keep him.
A public dig at one skipping jukebox repair stings a little but is soon fixed and forgotten.
The fixer who runs the street declared his work a failure to the whole bar, striking at the name his trade rests on.
Customers told to go elsewhere means less money for a stall already two months behind.
His one friend's trade was publicly trashed by the most powerful person on the grid, a real blow to Mux he will worry over.
The runner fetching glasses when asked barely registers.
Her own tenant announces to her bar that he is defecting to her rival, the very loss of belief that lets Vance move in.
Losing a tenant's rent is a small further dent while she is short on Kessler's money.
Right after announcing his defection, her tenant obeys her order and walks back to his stall in front of the room, restoring her face.
His friend's burned thumb is a trivial mishap he forgets at once.
His closest friend was maimed by men hunting him, a serious harm to someone he cares for.
The hunters have found the very room he sleeps in and have said they will return.
Five eddies off a 400 rent is a small, welcome easing that changes nothing about his arrears.
Setting his own prices without her checking is a noticed bit of freedom in running his stall.
The arrears that had his living and his daughter's home a month from being taken are wiped, and the stall is his for as long as Rogue runs the grid.
His skill is named as the thing that saved her money, a recognition he will remember.
A brushed trace that was probably cut is a small worry about heat she notes.
A corporate retrieval team now knows where her bar is and is coming tonight, putting her place and her life on the line.
Her feat of moving Kessler is named before the bar as something no one else manages.
Being toasted as the best fixer on the east side adds a little to her standing.
A free drink is a small pleasure that barely registers.
He can no longer pick his own work or set his own price, a real limit on his course.
The crew she owes is threatening to take the bar unless she walks into a midnight meeting alone.
She is being told where to be, when and how, on pain of losing the bar, a serious loss of her own choice.
A cell to power his own rig gives him a real way to work without Rogue's line.
Something worth real money in the hands of a man with 60 eddies is a small cushion.
His friend now has the means to run his own rig and stand a little freer of Rogue, which Mux will be glad of for days.
